history.prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a small mechanical assembly, studio render on a neutral seamless backdrop. A modular mechanical junction block with a single thick input routing into multiple diverging parallel output channels. Three recognizable engineered parts: a housing, a central distribution hub, and interlocking cable connectors. Matte surfaces with molding seams and soft contact shadows. Single soft key light, matte muted palette of soft gray and telecom orange. Generous negative space, clean editorial elegance.

style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Cinematic film still, anamorphic 35mm wide establishing composition. A massive industrial fiber optic routing bay inside an atmospheric data center, heavy brushed-steel server racks receding into deep shadow on the right. Thick bundles of glowing amber and teal fiber optic cables branch out from a central hardware switch in a complex, parallel fan-out configuration. Deep atmospheric volumetric haze, a single strong practical light source throwing dramatic directional shadows across the metallic rack panels. Restrained teal-and-amber color palette, quiet editorial restraint, moody architectural lighting.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, wordmarks, signage, UI, labels, watermark, logo, typography, people, human face, hands
rationale: A cinematic still of a physical routing bay grounds the abstract concept of 'agent wiring' in the tangible, high-cost reality of enterprise compute infrastructure, emphasizing the physical weight of computational cost.
subject: fiber optic routing bay with branching cables
alt_text: A massive fiber optic routing bay in a dark data center, with complex glowing cables branching out from a central switch.
caption: The topology of multi-agent systems dictates their compute cost, making wiring design a critical budget decision.
title: Multi-Agent Topology Routing
